report.summary: Reviewed chunk 10 of 11 of gated_writes.py, lines 1081-1155. Found docstring claims about never writing primary checkout, not calling promote_candidates, and coercing auto_promote. All claims are checkable and kept. Also observed governance blocking and legacy handling logic.
risks: held_by_task construction | low | held_by_task uses c.result.task_id but if task_id is None or duplicate, mapping may be incorrect; ensure task_id is always present and unique.
artifact_lost path | medium | When res.artifact_path is missing, status 'gated_artifact_lost' is set but res.persist_error may also be missing; error message could be unclear.
type ignore comment | low | 'type: ignore[return-value]' on return results suggests potential typing issue; may mask real errors.

claims.why: No write to primary checkout is performed in this chunk; writes are gated and held.
No call to promote_candidates appears in this chunk.

claims.text: Legacy ``auto_promote`` values are reported as denied input and coerced to ``"never"``
claims.why: Lines 1091-1092: if auto_promote not in AUTO_PROMOTE_LEVELS, it is set to 'never'. Additionally, line 1091 stores original in requested_auto_promote, and later (line 1142) adds key 'requested_auto_promote' to result dict if coercion occurred.

observations.what: Function run_write_wave has a docstring that makes three specific claims about its behavior; all are verifiable in this chunk.
Governance verdict can block promotion, causing all candidates to be held with a reason string that includes governance state and verdict.
When promotion is allowed, candidates are held with a message referencing 'sealed promotion' and optional legacy note.
The held_by_task dictionary is built from candidate results; if task_id is not unique, later entries overwrite earlier ones.
Result dict includes many fields conditionally; missing keys may cause downstream issues.
If res.artifact_path is missing after a successful gate, status 'gated_artifact_lost' is set with a reason that may include persist_error.
